hook.text: A robot the size of a washing machine weeds lettuce fields using computer vision. It works 24/7 without breaks.

buildup.text: Farm labor is increasingly scarce and expensive. In the US, labor shortages leave crops rotting in fields.

discovery.text: Companies like FarmWise and Carbon Robotics build autonomous machines that weed, thin, and harvest without humans.

twist.text: Laser weeding robots zap weeds with thermal energy—no herbicides needed. They kill 100,000 weeds per hour.

climax.text: Swarms of small robots could replace large tractors—lighter machines that don't compact soil.

punchline.text: The future farmer might manage a fleet of robots from a tablet. The field runs itself.

quiz.question: How do laser weeding robots kill weeds?
options: By zapping them with thermal energy—no chemicals needed

details.summary: Autonomous farm robots perform tasks like weeding, planting, harvesting, and monitoring without human operators. This topic covers robotic designs, computer vision, and how automation addresses farm labor shortages while improving precision.
details.whyItMatters: Farm labor shortages are worsening in developed countries. Autonomous robots can work around the clock, perform repetitive tasks with superhuman precision, and reduce dependency on seasonal workers.
takeaways: Weeding robots use computer vision to distinguish crops from weeds at millimeter scale
Autonomous harvesters pick delicate fruit like strawberries without bruising
Smaller robots reduce soil compaction compared to heavy conventional machinery

faq.question: What tasks can autonomous farm robots perform?
faq.answer: Farm robots can weed fields using precision lasers or mechanical tools, plant seeds at exact spacing, spray targeted micro-doses of herbicide, monitor crop health, harvest fruits and vegetables, and transport loads across the farm.

faq.question: How do farm robots identify and remove weeds?
faq.answer: Robots use high-resolution cameras and computer vision algorithms trained on thousands of plant images to distinguish weeds from crops in real time, then destroy weeds using targeted laser pulses, micro-sprays, or mechanical tools.
